sections.label: Banking Bill DBU ACU merchant banks
sections.summary: The Bill removes the requirement for banks to segregate accounting books into DBU and ACU, and consolidates merchant bank regulation under the Banking Act with a licensing regime.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: First, the Bill will remove the requirement for banks to segregate their accounting books into the Domestic Banking Unit (DBU) and the Asian Currency Unit (ACU).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The second change, the Bill will rationalise and consolidate the regulation of merchant banks under the Banking Act and subject them to a licensing regime, under which they will be licensed as a class of financial institutions distinct from banks.

sections.label: Enhanced global bank standards
sections.summary: Home regulators including Singapore will require banks to meet enhanced group-wide and global standards, including capital and liquidity buffer minimums, covering branches and subsidiaries in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: All home regulators, including Singapore, will now require their banks to meet enhanced standards on a group-wide and global basis, which include their branches and subsidiaries in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, for example, new global rules have raised the amount and quality of capital with the introduction of a minimum 4.5% Common Equity Tier 1 capital adequacy ratio requirement and have introduced minimum standards on the amount of liquidity buffers that banks need to hold.

sections.label: Consequential amendments removing DBU-ACU divide
sections.summary: The Bill removes the DBU-ACU divide and makes consequential amendments to the Banking Act on insolvency ranking, asset maintenance ratios and regulatory limits for foreign bank branches.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Therefore, the Bill will remove the DBU-ACU divide and make corresponding consequential amendments to the relevant provisions in the Banking Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: These include amendments to (a) rank uninsured non-bank deposits in insolvency by the currency denomination of the deposits, that is, Singapore dollar or a foreign currency, rather than by DBU or ACU; (b) apply asset maintenance ratios on Singapore dollar non-bank deposits, instead of DBU non-bank deposits; and (c) remove the regulatory limits imposed on the Singapore branches of foreign banks for equity investments, immovable property and large exposures.

sections.label: Merchant bank licensing framework
sections.summary: The Bill streamlines the regulatory framework for merchant banks by consolidating them under the Banking Act and introducing a new Part VIIB licensing framework.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As we remove the DBU-ACU divide, we are taking the opportunity to have the Bill also streamline the regulatory framework for merchant banks by consolidating them under the Banking Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill will introduce a new Part VIIB in the Banking Act to set out a new licensing framework for merchant banks as a class of financial institutions distinct from banks.

sections.label: Expanding MAS licence revocation grounds
sections.summary: It becomes necessary to expand the grounds for MAS to revoke a bank licence, enhance MAS' enforcement powers over banks and uphold trust in the financial system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As a result, it becomes necessary to expand the grounds for MAS to revoke a bank licence to better protect depositors, enhance MAS' enforcement powers over banks and uphold trust and confidence in our financial system.

sections.label: MAS powers over outsourcing arrangements
sections.summary: The new section empowers MAS to impose risk-proportionate, legally binding requirements on arrangements, including audit rights, customer information protection obligations and termination rights.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The new section will empower MAS to impose on such arrangements, risk-proportionate, legally binding requirements, such as requiring a bank to include in its agreements with the service providers: the right of MAS to audit the service provider; the obligations of the service providers to protect the customer information against unauthorised disclosure, retention or use; and the bank’s right to terminate the arrangement under specified circumstances.

sections.label: ACRA access to bank audit papers
sections.summary: The Banking Act Third Schedule is amended to let ACRA access complete bank audit working papers, including customer information, to review auditors more effectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Banks are audited by external auditors, but external auditors are, in turn, assessed by the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA), which evaluates the quality of the audits performed by the auditors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, ACRA is the auditor of the auditor.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, we are amending the Third Schedule of the Banking Act to allow ACRA access to complete bank audit working papers, which includes customer information, and that would enable ACRA to review the auditors more effectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For example, ACRA can evaluate if the external auditor has assessed the credit quality of customers and the adequacy of provisions appropriately, against market information.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This amendment will help raise the quality of bank audits and support MAS' supervision of banks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: ACRA officers with access to the information will be subject to confidentiality requirements.

sections.label: Revocation of bank licences
sections.summary: Amended section 20(1) expands grounds for revoking bank licences, allowing MAS to revoke a licence if satisfied it is in the public interest under section 20(1)(d).

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amended section 20(1) will expand the grounds for revocation of bank licences, allowing MAS to revoke a bank licence if it "is satisfied that it is in the public interest to do so" under section 20(1)(d).

sections.label: Approval of card licensees' controllers
sections.summary: Under new section 57FD, key appointment holders and 20% controllers of credit card or charge card licensees must be approved as fit and proper by MAS before appointment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, under the new section 57FD, key appointment holders and 20% controllers of credit card or charge card licensees are to be approved as "fit and proper" by MAS before being officially appointed.

sections.label: Senior management group family members
sections.summary: MAS has stated that the senior management group will include family members of the executive officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MAS has also stated that "senior management group" will include "family members of the executive officers".

sections.label: Documenting executive officer determinations
sections.summary: A question asks whether MAS will require in subsidiary legislation that banks document how they determine the list of executive officers, currently only recommended as good practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will MAS consider requiring in subsidiary legislation that banks document how they determine the list of "executive officer(s)" given that it is currently already recommended that banks do so but only as good practice?

sections.label: Australian wildfires land and claims
sections.summary: Ongoing wildfires in Australia have burnt through five million hectares of land, costing A$240 million in claims so far.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we speak, ongoing wildfires in Australia have burnt through five million hectares of land costing A$240 million in claims so far.

sections.label: Carbon emissions reporting and SGX
sections.summary: Facilities emitting over 2,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent report emissions to NEA, and such data should be used for carbon risk assessment and mandated for SGX-listed companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Facilities with higher than 2,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions report their emissions to the National Environment Agency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Such data should be used for carbon risk assessment and be mandated for reporting by Singapore Exchange (SGX)-listed companies.

sections.label: Singapore banks and international principles
sections.summary: Only one Singapore bank is a signatory to the Equator Principles and none has signed the UN Principles of Responsible Banking.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In terms of international alignment, we note that only one Singapore bank is a signatory to the Equator Principles and none has signed the United Nations (UN) Principles of Responsible Banking.

sections.label: Green investment needs and DBS funding
sections.summary: ASEAN green investments needed US$3 trillion between 2016 and 2030, and DBS provided S$2.4 billion of sustainable funding according to its 2018 Sustainability Report.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Green investments needed in the ASEAN region amounted to US$3 trillion between 2016 and 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As NGFS has noted, "the impacts of climate change could be irreversible, if not mitigated."’ According to their 2018 Sustainability Report, DBS provided S$2.4 billion of sustainable funding.

sections.label: Financial services share of GDP
sections.summary: Financial services directly contributed 13% to gross domestic product in 2018, or S$64 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Financial services directly contribute a significant 13% to our gross domestic product in 2018 or S$64 billion.

sections.label: MAS sandbox and environmental risk guidelines
sections.summary: MAS uses a regulatory sandbox approach and plans a 2020 public consultation to inform upcoming guidelines for Environmental Risk Assessment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MAS is also known for its "regulatory sandbox" approach, sometimes described as "regulation running alongside innovation".

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am aware MAS is planning a public consultation exercise in 2020 – earlier than later, I hope – to inform the upcoming, finally, guidelines for Environmental Risk Assessment.

sections.label: MAS bank licence revocation powers
sections.summary: MAS withdrew BSI Bank and Falcon Bank merchant bank status in 2016 for anti-money laundering breaches, and the Banking Act amendment extends the public interest ground to revoking bank licences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In 2016, MAS withdrew the merchant bank status of BSI Bank and Falcon Bank – both were merchant banks – because both banks had committed serious breaches of MAS' anti-money laundering requirements and there was gross misconduct by their management and staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Those powers were provided under the MAS Act in relation to merchant banks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This latest amendment to the Banking Act will extend the use of the public interest ground to the revocation of bank licences.

sections.label: Public interest bank licence revocations
sections.summary: The proposed public interest ground for bank licence revocations will be reserved for the most serious cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng can be assured that the proposed public interest ground for bank licence revocations will be reserved for the most serious of cases.

sections.label: Sustainable and resilient financial system
sections.summary: Ms Anthea Ong raised points on building a sustainable and resilient financial system, including green finance standards and technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Lastly, Ms Anthea Ong raised a few points on building a sustainable and resilient financial system, such as developing standards for green finance and leveraging technology and innovation to enhance sustainable finance efforts.

sections.label: MAS green finance action plan
sections.summary: MAS announced its green finance action plan in November 2019 at a FinTech festival with a big international audience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: MAS announced its green finance action plan in November 2019, at a FinTech festival with big international audience.

sections.label: Environmental risk management guidelines
sections.summary: MAS is not setting up national green banks and will issue environmental risk management guidelines, with a consultation paper in the first quarter of 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: To answer Ms Anthea Ong's question, we are not looking to specifically set up national green banks which are probably not necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For a start, MAS will be issuing environmental risk management guidelines to set out its supervisory expectations on governance, risk management and disclosure across the banking, insurance and asset management sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The consultation paper, as alluded to by Ms Anthea Ong, will be published in the first quarter of 2020.
